answer: Cipher-Linked Quorum Receipts. Each identity must publish a signed quill log of every coordination it joins; joining a new quorum requires referencing receipts from prior quorums, and a validator checks the log's hash chain. Fake identities form isolated clusters whose receipts never intersect the main graph, so their votes carry no weight. An attacker must run and maintain a distinct, active history per identity, costing real coordination work per sybil rather than a one-time jade payment.
